extracted.intended_audience: antiquarians, local historians, clergy, and general readers interested in ecclesiastical antiquities
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive standards for documenting and evaluating church fittings (bells, fonts, watching-chambers, and church chests), stressing features, inscriptions, symbolism, materials, placement, and prescribed procedures for custody of registers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bell inscriptions (form, language, and dating)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inscriptions on church bells — including names, devotional phrases, Latin legends, poetic couplets, and dates — are important features to record and interpret.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the inscription verbatim (e.g. 'Jhesus be our spede, 1590'; 'All men that heare my mournful sound, repent before you lye in ground, 1661'); note language (Lombardic capitals, corrupt Latin forms such as 'Som rosa polsata monde Maria vocata' = 'Sum Rosa pulsata mundi Maria vocata'), poetic content, and date. Provide translations or glosses where helpful and compare corrupt/variant spellings with known legend forms (example given and a French rendering by Mr. Sankey).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bell inscriptions as poetic/ didactic texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Many bells bear short poetic inscriptions that declare their functions (calling to church, summoning to the grave) or exhort listeners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When documenting a bell, transcribe any verse or motto (examples given: 'I to the church the living call, And to the grave do summons all.--1781'; 'My roaring sounde doth warning geve That men cannot heare always lyve.--1605') and note how the text reflects intended function (call to worship, funeral toll, moral exhortation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bells' musical/sonic character and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess bells by their tone and the setting in which they are heard: village and cathedral bells tend to have a poetic, mellifluous influence, while urban bells in densely populated industrial areas can be a nuisance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the tonal quality (mellifluous, brazen tintinnabulations, muffled, monotone), the musical effect (carillon, chimes), and the social context (village tower vs. town with night workers). Note reported emotional effects (poetical charm vs. depressing/irritating clangour) and any schedules of ringing that affect perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chiming repertoire and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the actual tunes and regular schedule used by chimes or peals, as these form part of a church's character and historical identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document named tunes and their assignment to days (example: All Saints' Church, Derby plays 'Old One Hundred and Fourth' on Sunday, 'The Lass of Patie's Mill' on Monday, etc.), and note historical origin or dating of repertoire (here 'they all date from the last century').

rubrics_metrics.name: Font typology and prominent design features
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify font types (canopied fonts, Seven Sacrament fonts, Posy fonts, leaden fonts, lion fonts, Decorated/Perpendicular/Decorated-period styles) and key design elements used to evaluate importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record canopy form and support (e.g. canopied fonts where canopy is supported by four massive posts), overall dignity and scale, presence and form of canopy (crocketed spire, pulley suspension), and notable local examples (S. Peter Mancroft, Sall, Elsing, Merton, Worstead).

rubrics_metrics.name: Iconography and symbolism on fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate fonts by the presence, subject, and arrangement of sculptured figures and symbolic motifs (e.g. panels representing sacraments, Evangelists, saints, beasts, and sin-symbols).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note the number and subjects of panels (example: Seven Sacrament fonts with seven panels depicting the Sacraments and an eighth showing the Crucifixion), figures on stem (four Evangelists and other saints), plinth form (Maltese cross noted), and symbolic animals or grotesques (double dragon, linked lions, dogs biting each other). Use these features to date and interpret theological emphasis (e.g. presence of two Sacraments of the Gospel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Font material, coloration, and rarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials (stone, lead) and traces of original colouration or unusual construction contribute to a font's significance and rarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record material (note leaden fonts as rare survivals—Brundall example), any surviving paint fragments (as at Upton), and unique features (Posy fonts bearing short inscriptions/posies like 'Thynk and Thank'). Note comparative scarcity and whether copies or reproductions exist (Crystal Palace copy of Walsingham font).

rubrics_metrics.name: Detail, workmanship, and musical/ornamental carving
rubrics_metrics.description: Richness of carving, technical execution, and presence of unusual carved details (musical instruments, open service books, figures in bas relief) are primary criteria for assessing a font's artistic value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the quality and intricacy of canopies, pinnacles, rose bosses, pediments, and bas-relief figures; record carved instruments (rebec, crowth, early fiddle) and other iconographic details. Note evidence of continental influence or guild-work and record any mutilation or later damage with associated dates scratched into linings (e.g. 1641, 1662, 1696).

rubrics_metrics.name: Function and placement of watching-chambers
rubrics_metrics.description: Watching-chambers (lofts/galleries/oriels) are to be identified by their placement and architectural openings which command views of altars/shrines and thereby serve security and surveillance functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record whether spaces provide elevated views of the church/shrine (sited to command a good view), presence of squints or tracery-filled fronts, two-storey carved timber structures with cupboards below and galleries above, stone lofts, rooms over north porches, and examples (S. Alban's, Christ Church Oxford, Bourges, Nuremberg, Westminster). Note dual explanations (guarding treasures vs. abbot's surveillance) and usage evidence ('abbot's pew').

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical requirements and practical rules for church chests and registers
rubrics_metrics.description: Documented procedural requirements for the custody of parish registers and the provision of secure chests are an authoritative standard for church repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote or summarize the seventieth canon and earlier visitation rules: parishes should 'provide one sure coffer, and three locks and keys; whereof one to remain with the minister, and the other two with the churchwardens severally; so that neither the minister without the two churchwardens, nor the churchwardens without the minister, shall at any time take that book out of the said coffer.' Also record the prescribed routine: 'upon every Sabbath day immediately after morning or evening prayer, the minister and the churchwardens shall take the said parchment book out of the said coffer, and the minister... shall write and record... names of all persons christened... married and buried... and that done, they shall lay up the book in the coffer as before.' Note provenance from Acts of 1538 and visitation orders (Grindal 1571/1576) and emphasize that strength, durability, and strong locks were the principal design aims of chests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Church chest construction and antiquity indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess chests by construction technique, materials, ironwork, and carpentry as clues to date and function (e.g. single-log hollowed coffers vs. later made hutches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record construction type (hollowed single log, iron-bound, panelled examples), roughness vs. elaborate workmanship (rudeness not definitive of great antiquity), and regional examples (Newdigate, Hales Owen, Clymping, Saltwood, Brancepeth). Emphasize that structural strength and strong locks/bolts are the main evaluative criteria for their intended protective function.
